contradictions.fact: Bivy list includes camps for other Glacier Peak routes/peaks, and one entry denies this route's own approach still exists

claims.says: Describes and uses the White Chuck River Trailhead -> Kennedy Hot Springs -> Sitkum Creek -> Boulder Basin approach as the route's current (if road-walk-extended) access

claims.field: bivy[8] ("Boulder Basin above Sitkum Creek — and the White Chuck situation")
claims.says: "Anything you read describing five and a half easy miles to the hot springs and a steep climbers' path to the basin is describing an approach that has not been available for twenty years. Parties wanting the north and west sides of the mountain now go in from the Suiattle instead."

Mackinaw Shelter, White Pass, Glacier Gap, Kennedy Ridge, Buck Creek Pass, Napeequa Valley, Butterfly Butte and Boulder Pass/Thunder Basin entries all describe camps for entirely different peaks/routes (Glacier Peak's Cool Glacier/Gerdine Ridge and Kennedy Glacier routes, Buck Mountain, Mount Berge, Helmet Butte, Clark Mountain, Luahna Peak, Chalangin Peak, Tenpeak Mountain) with no connection to this route's own White Chuck approach

contradictions.why: The CAMPING & BIVY section would show a climber camps for eight unrelated peaks reached from different trailheads, and one of those entries flatly states the very approach this route's own approach/road/waypoints/itinerary describe using no longer exists.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The route's own approach, road, access, waypoints and itinerary all consistently describe using the White Chuck Trailhead approach today (with an added road-walk detour around the FR 23 closure); that is corroborated 5+ times and is clearly the intended route data. The bivy array appears to be a generic area-wide camp dump pasted onto the route rather than filtered to it.

contradictions.fact: Best/optimal season window extends past the stated season

claims.says: "Jun-Aug"
"July through September, with July offering the most stable snow bridges and weather and September trading some glacier stability for shorter, cooler days"
"Late July through early September is the most reliable window..."
"Warmest, driest window (late July-early September)..."
"good" (within best season)

contradictions.why: The short-form header season caps at August, but three other fields (seasonal_guidance, best_season, climate) all treat September as part of the good/optimal window — a best window may lie inside a stated season, but here the optimal window runs outside it.
contradictions.internal_resolution: Three independent fields agree September belongs in the season; only the single `season` string omits it, so `season` is the likely outlier.

contradictions.fact: dist_km is one-way while itinerary is the round trip

claims.says: 14.5 (≈9.0 mi, matches the one-way distance to Boulder Basin)
"roughly 25-mile round trip"

contradictions.why: dist_km and the itinerary describe different quantities (one-way approach vs. full round trip); the header shows itinerary miles when present, so they are unlikely to be shown side-by-side, but noting per instructions.

"For GOTHIC PEAK this costs almost nothing... while for DEL CAMPO it does cost you... Getting here means the Weden Creek trail..."

contradictions.internal_resolution: The first bivy entry ("Sunrise Mine road end") and the last ("Red Bridge Campground") explicitly name Sperry and match its own approach; the Gothic Basin/Weden Creek entries are the contaminated outliers.

contradictions.fact: Road-closure detour mileage: 16.1 mi one-way mislabeled as "16 miles round trip"

claims.says: Closure at milepost 4.5; trailhead normally at milepost 20.6 (waypoints[0])
"...the current washout closure at MP 4.5 adds roughly 16 miles round trip of road walking or biking to reach the Downey Creek trailhead."

contradictions.why: 20.6 − 4.5 = 16.1 miles one-way; the round trip should be roughly 32 miles, not 16 — the text computes the one-way distance but labels it round trip, understating the extra approach distance by about half.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The mileposts given in the same field (4.5 to 20.6) arithmetically yield ~16 miles one-way / ~32 round trip; "16 miles round trip" is inconsistent with its own inputs.

contradictions.fact: Road-washout location stated inconsistently (mile 4.8 vs. mile 8/8.5)

claims.says: "Tupso Pass Road (FS 41) washed out 4.8 miles in (past Canyon Creek bridge at mile 8); permanently closed to vehicles."
"...washed out ~4.8 miles in and closed to vehicles beyond the Canyon Creek bridge (~mile 8.5) since 2023."
"Washed out at approximately mile 4.8; permanently closed to vehicle travel beyond the Canyon Creek bridge (~mile 8.5)"
All state the closure adds "roughly 9 miles each way" to reach the trailhead at mile ~17.5-18, which is only consistent with a closure point at mile ~8.5, not 4.8

contradictions.why: access.notes literally claims the mile-8 bridge lies "past" the 4.8-mile washout point, which is mathematically impossible (4.8 < 8); three fields conflate a "mile 4.8" figure with the "mile 8/8.5" Canyon Creek bridge closure point in the same breath, while the consistently-used "9 miles each way" road-walk figure only works from mile ~8.5.
contradictions.internal_resolution: road.driveNote, itinerary.cal and the trailhead waypoint's directions all independently and consistently compute "~9 miles each way" from a closure at ~mile 8.5 to the trailhead at ~mile 17.5-18; the "4.8 miles in" figure appearing in access.notes/access.closures/road.status is the outlier and is not used anywhere else in the route's own mileage math.
